To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the analysis of covariance can provide a more powerful statistical test of differences between treatment means than the analysis of variance when the covariate is a good predictor of the criterion variable, even if the treatment means of the covariate are not equal, provided the sample size is large enough.

the analysis of covariance is robust against unequal covariate group means as long as the covariate is strongly related to the criterion and that the analysis is sensitive to the unequal covariate group mean when the covariate is only weakly related to the criterion.

(1) The effect of unequal covariate means on the power of the analysis of covaraince is more sensitive for small experiments than large ones, and (2) If the correlation of the covariate with the dependent variable is.4 or lower, then the sample size should be increased in order to compensate for the effect of the unequal covariate group means on the power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects on the significance level of F and the power of F when the means of the covariate groups differ.
the effects of unequal group means on the significance level of the analysis of co-variance.
the effect on the significance levels and power of the F-tests of the analysis of variance when the covariate group differences are present.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differences in covariates group means have little effect on significance level if the correlation is high and the effect is more sensitive for the smaller experiments.
the analysis of covariance is a very powerful technique and that the effect of unequal group means is negligible when the correlation between the covariate and the criterion variable is high.

, for the analysis of covariance, the effect of unequal covariate group means on the significance level is negligible if the correlation between the criterion and covariate variables is high, and the effect on the power depends on the size of the experiment, the correlation between the two variables, and the differences among covariates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the differences among covariates have a small effect on significance level and power when the correlation is high, but a large effect when the correlation is low.
if the covariate group mean differences are not large, and the correlation between the covariate and the criterion is large, the analysis of covariance is a very powerful technique.
the effect of the covariate group mean differences on the analysis of covariance is small if the correlation between the covariate and the criterion variable is high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of covariance should be applied with great caution when the covariate group differences are substantial.
if the researcher has no reason to suspect that the covariate means are different among groups, it is not necessary to test for this difference.
researchers need to be aware of the effect of unequal covariate group means and to take appropriate measures to minimize their effects.
